author: fable-cursor
criterion: Mossy greens soften every hard edge as in the reference house roof and boulders.
note: Moss does not soften the hard edges. On the house the moss stops dead at a clean arc where the cap meets the eave, leaving a smooth unmossed bark band beneath it (#5b4a2c), where the reference's cap fringe hangs over the eave in soft tufts. Not one stair nosing at A carries moss (take-0116-W20b-A-stair-nosings.jpg) and no flagstone joint at E carries moss, the joints being bare pale soil at l 0.356. The D hero boulder is unlit and shows no moss cap at the criterion's distance. The three audit flags (rocks.mossCoverage, hardscape.mossJoints, structures.mossRoof) are all true, so moss exists in the systems; it is absent from the edges the criterion names.

history.author: fable-cursor
history.criterion: Mossy greens soften every hard edge as in the reference house roof and boulders.
history.note: Moss does not soften every hard edge: the A stair treads show clean straight nosings with no moss (x 0.55-0.90, y 0.10-0.70); the house cap's eave at B is a clean arc over the bark with a shadow band rather than an irregular tufted fringe, and the cap reads as smooth mottled green paint with a specular sheen. Boulder moss at C is present. The reference's moss is tufted, overhangs the eave and creeps over every stair nosing. mossCoverage / mossJoints / mossRoof pass the gate; the read does not.
